## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Loaded data

```{r}
stoke_data <- read.csv("data/healthcare.csv")
```

4 Visualizations

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r}
ggplot(data = stoke_data, aes(x = stroke, fill = factor(hypertension))) +
  geom_bar(position = 'dodge')　+
  theme_bw()
```

```{r}
ggplot(data = stoke_data, aes(x = factor(stroke), fill = factor(stroke), y = avg_glucose_level)) +
  geom_boxplot()
```

```{r}
ggplot(data = stoke_data, aes(x = heart_disease, fill = factor(gender))) +
  geom_bar(position = 'dodge')　+
  theme_bw()
```

P(A) : Probability of Heartdisease

```{r}
probability_of_heart_disease <- data |> 
  count(heart_disease) |> 
  mutate(percent = n / sum(n)) |> 
  filter(heart_disease == 1) |> 
  pull(percent)

# 0.054
```

P(B) : Probability of stroke

```{r}
probability_of_stroke <- data %>% 
  count(stroke) %>% 
  mutate(percent = n / sum(n)) %>% 
  filter(stroke == 1) %>% 
  pull(percent)

# 0.048
```

```{r}
data |>  
  ggplot(aes(x = gender, fill = heart_disease)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  labs(
    title = "Stroke Count by Heart Disease",
    x = "Gender", y = "Number of Patients", fill = "Stroke Status"
  )
```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
#| echo: false
2 * 2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).
